questions: Can the edge reversal operation be performed multiple times, and if so, does each reversal toggle the direction of all edges (i.e., flipping them back and forth) or does it set them to a fixed reversed orientation regardless of previous reversals?
When reversing edges, is the reversal applied to the current state of the graph (i.e., after previous moves and reversals) or always to the original graph's edges?
Is the cost X incurred each time the reversal operation is performed, regardless of whether it changes the graph state (e.g., if edges are already reversed)?
Are self-loops (edges where u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, can moving along such an edge keep you at the same vertex while incurring cost 1?
Can you perform the reversal operation while at any vertex, including vertex N (even though the goal is to reach N, but what if you overshoot or reverse after arriving)?
Is the graph allowed to have multiple edges between the same pair of vertices in the same direction, and if so, does moving along one count as a single move with cost 1?
Does the reversal operation affect all edges globally immediately, or is there a delay (e.g., applied only after the move)?
If you reverse edges, then move, then reverse again, does the second reversal revert to the original orientation or flip the current reversed orientation?
